reason: The text depicts Moses, the Hebrew leader, consistently supporting and protecting the Hebrew people. When they cry out in fear at the approaching Egyptian forces, Moses encourages them ('Do not fear, stand firm and see the salvation of the Lord') and assures them that God will fight for them. Moses then performs the miraculous parting of the Red Sea, enabling the Israelites to escape. These actions demonstrate protection and alignment with the people's welfare, not antagonism. While the people voice complaints and fear about their circumstances, the Hebrew leadership shown in this passage acts in the people's interest, not against them.
